ai.description: This large frog reaches 70–80 mm. It is brown with a pale snout and granular skin. Key features include prominent, fleshy, triangular toe tips and a distinct, rounded snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus grandis* is distinguished by its exceptionally large, robust body size and the presence of prominent, fleshy, triangular toe tips compared to smaller congeners.
ai.habitat: The Wayanad Night Frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and riparian zones in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Wayanad Night Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden in rock crevices or under leaf litter during the day and emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus grandis* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying terrestrial clutches of 30–50 eggs on rocks or vegetation near streams, which undergo direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Wayanad Night Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting the Wayanad region of Kerala at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Wayanad Night Frog produces a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard emanating from rocky streams within its humid forest habitat.
